metrics.meta_harness_gate_catch_rate_method: distinct defect classes named across ALL families' defects_found history as of this run, vs. how many now have a LANDED, automated, pre-coordinator-review check (a validator gate or fitness function), not merely a fix authored or a human review that caught it once. Six classes on record: (A) mint capture-incompleteness, (B) mint unicode/transcription corruption undetected by intra-payload check, (C) screen round-1 per-row data loss, (D) screen round-2 99-row misclassification, (E) fetch-drain host-level timeout/hang, (F) fetch-drain *.gov.au HTTP/2 stream-error cluster. Gated as of this run: A and B only (validate-mint-payload.mjs's new capture-completeness and unicode-integrity checks, this wave) = 2/6. NOT counted as gated: C (structurally prevented by run-numbered filenames, a different mechanism than a pre-review CONTENT check — screen-worklist.mjs can no longer silently overwrite a prior round's output, but nothing checks a row's CLASSIFICATION before it lands); D (fixed by a one-time human mechanism-test re-audit, no automated rule change); E (fix authored, commit 0735a410, but NOT DEPLOYED as of this run); F (fix_ref: null, unresolved). This is a small-N (6), cumulative, retrospective count — not a statistically meaningful rate — recomputed fresh at each meta-harness run, not asserted once.

defects_found.description: MH-3 makes batch-001's capture-incompleteness defect class structurally IMPOSSIBLE to pass silently (6/6 payloads now correctly rejected), but does not make any of the six payloads structurally CORRECT — re-fetching them under the new slice-and-rebuild law so they actually PASS the hardened validator is explicitly deferred ('M2 full-text rebuild + apply batch-001 UNDER the hardened validator,' build plan §4). At the meta-harness level this is worth naming precisely rather than reading 'defect fixed' as 'data fixed': a gate that reliably rejects a known-bad class is a real, measurable win, and a distinct thing from the underlying data being repaired.
defects_found.root_cause: explicit scope boundary stated plainly in mint-run-002.json's own config.retrofit and proposer_notes, not an oversight this run is newly discovering.

defects_found.description: The gate-catch-rate improvement (0/6 → 2/6) is entirely concentrated in the mint family. Screen's and fetch-drain's defect classes have zero landed automated gates as of this run: screen's is a human mechanism-review item by design (screen-run-003.json's own hard rule — never silently flip a decided verdict, so a rule change needs a dedicated mechanism-test pass, not a mechanical gate); fetch-drain's timeout fix is authored but undeployed, and its HTTP/2 class is unresolved. One family's live proposer-implementation cycle is driving the entire system's gate-catch rate — worth watching as a trend, not read as system-wide progress.
defects_found.root_cause: mint had a live implementation-scoped lane this wave (MH-3); screen's and fetch-drain's most recent proposer passes (MH-2, per their own LAST-PROPOSER-PASS.md) were 'none warranted' and 'deploy pending' respectively — neither was an implementation cycle.
